## Verdict: REJECT (a test this PR edited now claims coverage it does not have, and one important checklist failure)

This PR is not ready to merge: one test it edited has a name that is no longer true, and one doc sentence it edited says the `TABLE t` guard refuses every case when the code lets one input form through.

Rule applied: self-contradicting-diff carve-out — a test the PR's own diff modified makes an untrue claim → REJECT; rule 1 (a checklist FAIL at or above the threshold → REJECT) also matches.

## Code Review Findings

### 🟠 Important / Major

- VC-45: FAIL (important) — uses_table_shorthand flags every unquoted TABLE keyword except one directly after `.` or after an unquoted command keyword listed in _TABLE_KEYWORD_NOT_SHORTHAND_AFTER, refusing TABLE t in any statement or subquery. [docs/internal/database-connectors/read-only-safety.md:221]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Positive part holds: readonly.py:112-121 returns True for any TokenType.TABLE token whose preceding token text (uppercased, '' after a quoted identifier or string) is not in _TABLE_KEYWORD_NOT_SHORTHAND_AFTER (readonly.py:53-76). `WITH x AS (SELECT 1) TABLE x` has previous ')' and `(TABLE t) x` has previous '(', so both are flagged; whole_row.py:124 turns that into 'TABLE' and assert_no_whole_row_select raises WholeRowSelectError (whole_row.py:115-116). But the absolute wording 'refusing TABLE t in any statement or subquery' / 'unquoted command keyword' is not what the code does. The exemption is a pure text match on the previous token (readonly.py:120, `previous = token.text.upper()`), with no check that the token is acting as a command keyword. Counterexample input (MySQL): `INSERT INTO temp TABLE orders` (also `... INTO checksum|truncate|temporary|virtual|unlogged TABLE orders`). Here `temp` is an unquoted table name, not a command keyword. Its text 'TEMP' is in the set, so the TABLE token is skipped and uses_table_shorthand returns False. That contradicts the doc line (read-only-safety.md:221) 'flags every unquoted TABLE keyword except one directly after `.` or an unquoted command keyword' and 'refused ... in any statement'. Reach: `INSERT ... TABLE s` is valid MySQL, and the SQL is model-generated. The statement only gets past the read-only guard when database.read_only=false, which the doc covers at line 227. Whether the tree-based star check still catches it depends on how the installed sqlglot parses it (before 30.30 `TABLE orders` is not a SELECT), and I could not run sqlglot (no dependency_sources given), so the effect beyond uses_table_shorthand is unsettled. The claim's refusal guarantee is still wrong at the subject, uses_table_shorthand. Also in the set: EXPLAIN/ANALYZE/DESC etc. are intentional and documented in the code comment (readonly.py:46-52), so `EXPLAIN TABLE t` is a deliberate exception and not counted here.

  </details>
